summary_findings: Both languages carry the whole 27-fold nakṣatra system in their own phonology — Kittel enters all twenty-seven as Kannada headwords (ನಕ್ಷತ್ರ, p. 879: 'a constellation, an asterism in the moon's path, a lunar mansion, of which 27 (or 28) are enumerated'), and Brown does the same for Telugu (నక్షత్రము, p. 628) — so the tadbhava forms ಆರಿದ್ರ āridra, ಚಿತ್ತೆ citte, ಪುಬ್ಬೆ/ಹುಬ್ಬೆ pubbe/hubbe, ಜೇಟೆ jēṭe, ಮಘೆ maghe, ಸಾತಿ sāti and their Telugu twins చిత్త citta, పుబ్బ pubba, జెష్ట jeṣṭa are recorded here only as representative specimens. The real find is that TELUGU HAS A COMPLETE PARALLEL SET OF ITS OWN DESCRIPTIVE NAMES for the mansions, formed X-cukka / X-rikka 'X-star' or X-rūpu-rikka 'X-shaped star', which Brown scatters across the dictionary under their first elements and which no one has assembled: tolu-rikka and gurrapu-cukka (Aśvinī), baraṇi-cukka (Bharaṇī), kattera 'scissors' and mangala-katti-rūpu 'barber's-razor shape' (Kṛttikā), baṇḍi-rikka 'cart star' (Rohiṇī), jābili-rikka 'moon star' (Mṛgaśiras), pagaḍapu-rikka 'coral star' (Ārdrā — and Ārdrā is Betelgeuse, which is red), podariṇḍla-cukka (Punarvasu), poṭla-pū-cukka 'snake-gourd-flower star' (Puṣya), sappapu-cukka 'serpent star' and the frankly colloquial asilēru (Āśleṣā), petarula-cukka 'ancestors' star' and jannapu-cukka 'sacrifice star' (Maghā), sāmu-kaṇṭi-cukka (Pūrva-Phalgunī), proddu-rikka 'sun star' (Uttara-Phalgunī), muttepu-rikka 'pearl star' (Citrā = Spica, white), karuvali-rikka 'wind star' (Svāti), kummara-sāre-cukka 'potter's-wheel star' and jōḍu-vēlpula-rikka 'star of the paired gods' (Viśākhā), tāṭi-rikka 'palmyra star' (Jyeṣṭhā), sōku-cukka 'demon star' (Mūla — and Brown's own next line glosses sōkula-rēḍu 'lord of demons' as mūla-rēḍu), nīṭi-rikka 'water star' (Pūrvāṣāḍhā) beside nīṭi-rēni-rikka 'water-KING's star' (Śatabhiṣaj), maddela-rūpu-rikka 'drum-shaped star' (Dhaniṣṭhā), mukkaṇṭi-cukka 'the three-eyed one's star' (Uttara-Bhādrapadā), and three for Revatī: mīnu-rūpu-rikka 'fish-shaped', kona-rikka 'the last star' (answering tolu-rikka 'the first'), muppadi-reṇṭi gumpu 'the group of thirty-two'. Some are calques on the presiding deity, some are shape or colour names owing nothing to Sanskrit, and several also name the month (proddu-rikka-nela = Phālguna, tāṭi-rikka-nela = Jyeṣṭha, poṭla-pū-rikka-nela = Pauṣa), which shows the set worked as a calendar. KANNADA HAS NO SUCH SET: Kittel records only the tadbhava names, and attaches the popular material to them instead as rain proverbs (ಹುಬ್ಬೇ ಮಳೆ ಗುಬ್ಬೀ ತಲೆ ನೆನೆಯುವುದಿಲ್ಲ; ಮಖೆಮೞೆ ಆದರೆ ಮೊಗ ತೊಳೆಯುವದಕ್ಕೆ ಆಗದೇ?) and to the seasonal ಆರಿದ್ರಪುಱು, the ladybird of the Ārdrā rains, for which Kittel gives the Telugu ఆరుద్రపురుగు as an exact equivalent. The shared Dravidian layer lies elsewhere, in the generic and cosmological words, and it pairs up almost item for item: Te. cukka ~ Ka. cikki/cukke (both 'dot' before 'star'); Te. cukkala-teruvu 'street of the stars = sky' ~ Ka. mīn-vaṭṭe / aṟil-vaṭṭe / tārage-vaṭṭe 'star-road = sky'; Te. cukkala-rēḍu 'king of the stars = the moon' ~ Ka. mīngaḷ-eṟeya and tārageyāḷma, same sense; Te. tōka-cukka 'tail star = comet' ~ Ka. bāla-cikki, same compound with each language's own word for tail. Two Dravidian words split the languages: Kannada mīn is 'star' outright ('a fish of the sky-ocean?', Kittel's own guess, p. 1328) where Telugu mīnu is only 'fish' and touches the sky solely in mīnu-rūpu-rikka; and Kannada beḷḷi 'silver' is the name of Venus (with Tamil and Malayalam veḷḷi) where Telugu kept only the metal and named Venus vēgu-cukka 'dawn star'. Kannada also has an indigenous Milky Way that Sanskrit does not suggest — bāṅ-keṟe 'the sky-TANK', beside bāṅ-kaḍal 'sky-sea' and bān-toṟe 'sky-river' — the irrigation tank of the Karnataka countryside put in the sky, and Kittel's illustrative verse has the stars vanishing in it like diving fish. Telugu's milk-track names (pāla-punta, pāla-bāṭa) are not in Brown at all and are attested here only from Gwynn 1991. The agricultural sky is vernacular in both: Telugu kārte, marked [Tel.] by Brown, is the sun's thirteen-day stay in each asterism and the unit of the Deccan farming year, and Thurston records the working system for Lingāyat cultivators of Bellary — cholam on the Rohiṇi, Mṛgaśira and Ārdrā rains, cotton and horse gram on Pubba and Uttara, no weeding in Maghā, no lightning in Svāti. Telugu punāsa, the year's first inferior crop, is Punarvasu with the sky worn off it entirely. NEGATIVE FINDINGS, all of them from exhaustive searching of both dictionaries: neither language has any Dravidian name for URSA MAJOR — no plough, no cart, no bier, no seven sisters, only saptarṣi and citraśikhaṇḍi in both; none for ORION or Orion's Belt (Kittel's ilvalegaḷ is Sanskrit Ilvalāḥ with a Kannada plural; āgrahāyaṇi is a tatsama); none for CANOPUS (Agastya in both); none for SIRIUS in Telugu at all, and in Kannada only Sanskrit lubdhaka — which in Kannada lexicography usually means Ārdrā, not Sirius, a trap flagged in the entry; none for the POLE STAR beyond Dhruva, though Kannada has the popular dhruva-pāśa, the rope the earth hangs from; and no Dravidian PLEIADES name in Kannada, where Telugu has two. Brown twice calls Arundhatī 'a star in the Pleiades', which is wrong and is recorded as disputed because he may be reporting a real popular misidentification — Thurston shows the same star being called the pole star in south Indian weddings.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: The ordinary Telugu word for a star, and the second element of most of the language's own star-names (X-cukka). Brown lists the astronomical sense third, after 'mark' and 'drop'.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. చుక్క ṭsukka, p. 449
entries.quote: చుక్క [Tel.] n. Any small mark; a dot or spot: a drop, a small quantity of liquid. బొట్టు. The round mark (తిలకము) worn on the forehead by Hindus. A star, నక్షత్రము. The planet Venus, శుక్రుడు. A pip on the dice or cards. A comet. తోకచుక్క.
entries.notes: HOMONYM WARNING. cukka is 'dot / spot / drop' before it is 'star', and in ordinary Telugu prose the non-astronomical sense is far commoner (cukka-boṭṭu 'forehead mark', cukkani 'rudder'). Brown's entry is quoted at length precisely because the string 'A star, నక్షత్రము. The planet Venus, శుక్రుడు' inside it is what fixes the astronomical sense. Kannada ಚುಕ್ಕೆ cukke / ಚಿಕ್ಕಿ cikki is the exact cognate and carries the same ambiguity.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: The other native Telugu star-word, used almost exclusively as the second element of compound asterism names (baṇḍi-rikka, tāṭi-rikka, nīṭi-rikka …). Rarer than cukka as a free word.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. రిక్క rikka, p. 1085
entries.quote: రిక్క [Tel.] n. A star. నక్షత్రము. A constellation, a lunar mansion. A peculiar noise made in driving cattle. పశువులను తోలునపుడు చేయు ధ్వని. A pustule, weal, blister. బొబ్బ.
entries.notes: sanskrit_db_id deliberately left null. rikka descends from Sanskrit ṛkṣa through a Middle-Indic rikkha, but the only ṛkṣa entry in the Sanskrit database (id 'rksha') is the Vedic asterism = Ursa Major, which is not what Telugu rikka means. HOMONYM: Brown's same headword also covers a cattle-driving call and a blister.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: The learned word beside native cukka; the derivative tārā-pathamu 'starry path' is the standard Telugu word for the firmament.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. తార tāra, p. 523
entries.quote: తార [Skt.] n. A star. నక్షత్రము. The pupil of the eye, కనుగ్రుడ్డు, కనీనిక. … తారాపథము tārā-pathamu. n. The starry path, i.e., the firmament. ఆకాశము. తారావళి tārā-vaḷi. n. A constellation, or set of stars. The starry firmament.
entries.notes: Telugu tārā-pathamu is the direct counterpart of Sanskrit tārāpatha (db id 'tarapatha'). Brown flags the word [Skt.], i.e. tatsama.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: The almanac word. Brown glosses it back into the vernacular with చుక్క, which is the neatest single demonstration that the two registers are in use side by side.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. నక్షత్రము nakshatramu, p. 628
entries.quote: నక్షత్రము [Skt.] n. A star. చుక్క. A constellation. The name of any one of the twenty lunar mansions. అశ్విని మొదలగు నక్షత్రములు. … నక్షత్రేశుడు lit: the lord of the stars, i.e., the moon. చుక్కలరేడు. … నక్షత్రవీధి nakshatra-vīdhi. n. The Milky Way.
entries.notes: 'twenty' is a misprint in Brown for twenty-seven. Note that Brown twice supplies a vernacular equivalent for a Sanskrit compound (nakṣatra = cukka; nakṣatreśuḍu = cukkala-rēḍu).

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: Poetic register only.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. ఉడువు uḍuvu, p. 153
entries.quote: ఉడువు … A lunar mansion, a star. నక్షత్రము. ఉడుపతి or ఉడుపుడు uḍu-pati n: The lord of the stars, i.e., the moon చంద్రుదు. ఊడుగణము uḍu-gaṇamu. n. A constellation. ఉడువీధి. The heavens. ఉడుతతి uḍu-tati. n. The constellations.
entries.notes: Telugu uḍuvu = Sanskrit uḍu with the Telugu nominative suffix.

entries.sky_object: the sky, as the road of the stars
entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: A wholly Dravidian compound for the firmament; teruvu is 'street, road'.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. చుక్క ṭsukka, p. 449
entries.quote: చుక్కలతెరువు the sky ఆకాశము. చుక్కలరేడు the moon.
entries.notes: COGNATE PAIR. This is the exact structural twin of Kannada ಮೀನ್ವಟ್ಟೆ mīnvaṭṭe / ಅಱಿಲ್ವಟ್ಟೆ aṟilvaṭṭe / ತಾರಗೆವಟ್ಟೆ tāragevaṭṭe, all 'star-road = sky' (Kittel pp. 1328, 105, 752). Both languages inherit the figure independently of Sanskrit tārāpatha, which uses the same image.

entries.sky_object: the moon, as king of the stars
entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: Given by Brown twice — under cukka and as the vernacular gloss of Sanskrit nakṣatreśuḍu.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. చుక్క ṭsukka, p. 449
entries.quote: చుక్కలతెరువు the sky ఆకాశము. చుక్కలరేడు the moon.
entries.notes: COGNATE PAIR with Kannada ಮೀನ್ಗಳೆಱೆಯ mīngaḷeṟeya 'the moon' (lit. lord of the stars/fishes, Kittel p. 1328) and ತಾರಗೆಯಾಳ್ಮ tārageyāḷma (Kittel p. 752). The kenning 'lord of stars' is shared with Sanskrit but the words are Dravidian throughout.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: The classical Kannada word for a star is the word for a fish. Kittel's own guess at the motivation is printed in the entry.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಮೀನ್ mīn 2, p. 1328
entries.quote: ಮೀನ್ mīn. 2. (= ಮೀನ್ 1, a fish of the sky-ocean ?). = ಮೀಮ್ 2. a star (ನಕ್ಷತ್ರ Śmd. II; ತಾರಗೆ Ct. I, 46; ಅಱಿಲ್, ತಾರಗೆ, ನಕ್ಷತ್ರ Kk. 10b; ಅಱಿಲ್, ನಕ್ಷತ್ರ 80; ಅಱಿಲ್, ತಾರಗೆ, ತಾರೆ Śm. 16; ಭಗಣ 99 …) 2, glittering … — ಮೀನ್ಗಳೆಱೆಯ. -ಎಱೆಯ. the moon … — ಮೀನ್ವಟ್ಟೆ. -ಬಟ್ಟೆ. the sky (ಆಕಾಶ Kk. 12).
entries.notes: The most important non-Sanskrit sky-word in Kannada. It is the same mīn that Tamil uses for star, and it has no Sanskrit counterpart at all — the Sanskrit db id given is only the semantic equivalent nakṣatra, which is how Kittel's Kannada nighaṇṭu sources gloss it. Telugu kept mīnu strictly as 'fish': Brown p. 996 gives no astronomical sense for it except in the compound mīnu-rūpu-rikka (Revatī).

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: A second, purely Dravidian, classical Kannada star-word; obsolete in the modern language and known mainly from the old lexicons Kittel cites.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಅಱಿಲ್ aṟil 1, p. 105
entries.quote: ಅಱಿಲ್ ar̤il. 1. = ಅಱಲು. a star (ನಕ್ಷತ್ರ Śmd. II; ಮೀನ್, ತಾರಗೆ, ನಕ್ಷತ್ರ Kk. 10 b.; ಮೀನ್, ನಕ್ಷತ್ರ 80; ಮೀನ್, ತಾರೆಗೆ, ತಾರೆ, ತಾರಕೆ Śm. 16. 106). -ಅಱಿಲ್ವಟ್ಟೆ. -ಬಟ್ಟೆ the star-road: the sky (ಮೀನ್ವಟ್ಟೆ etc., ಆಕಾಶ Kk. 12; ಅಮ್ಬರ, ಬಾನ್, ಎಲರ್ವಟ್ಟೆ, ಆಗಸ, ಸಗ್ಗಿಗವಟ್ಟೆ Śm. 14).
entries.notes: HOMONYM: Kittel's very next headword ಅಱಿಲ್ 2 is 'mud, clay'. The compound aṟil-vaṭṭe 'star-road = sky' is the Kannada twin of Telugu cukkala-teruvu.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: The colloquial modern Kannada word (also ಚುಕ್ಕಿ cukki, ಚುಕ್ಕೆ cukke, ಚಿಕ್ಕೆ cikke), cognate with Telugu cukka.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಚಿಕ್ಕಿ cikki 2, p. 643
entries.quote: ಚಿಕ್ಕಿ cikki. 2. = ಚಿಕ್ಕೆ, ಚುಕ್ಕಿ, ಚುಕ್ಕೆ. a spot, a speck, a dot, as that of a cat, of a leopard, of a horse, of a cloth, etc. (C.). 2, a star (C.).
entries.notes: COGNATE PAIR with Telugu చుక్క cukka, and with the same dot/star polysemy in both languages. Kittel's parallel entry ಚುಕ್ಕೆ cukke (p. 653) reads 'a small mark, a dot, etc. (My.; Te.; T. ಚುಕ್ಕೈ, a star)' — i.e. he marks the star sense as Tamil and Telugu, the dot sense as the Kannada default.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: A trap for the unwary: Kittel has two homographic headwords ಚುಕ್ಕಿ. The one meaning 'star/dot' is Dravidian; this one, meaning the planet Venus, is a tadbhava of Sanskrit Śukra.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಚುಕ್ಕಿ cukki 2, p. 653
entries.quote: ಚುಕ್ಕಿ cukki. Tbh. of ಶುಕ್ರ. Śukra, the planet Venus and the preceptor of the daityas or rākṣasas (My.; ರಕ್ಕಸರ ಓಜ, ಅಸುರ ಗುರು Si. 17). see Prv. s. ತುರುಕ. -ಚುಕ್ಕಿಗುವರ. -ಕುವರ. a son or pupil of Śukra: a daitya
entries.notes: HOMONYM WARNING, and the reason this database tags register rather than assuming it. Kannada ಚುಕ್ಕಿ cukki 'star' (Dravidian, = Telugu cukka) and ಚುಕ್ಕಿ cukki 'Venus' (< Skt. Śukra) are separate words that fell together. Kittel keeps them as separate numbered headwords on the same page; the Sanskrit-derived one must NOT be counted as a vernacular Venus name. The genuinely vernacular Kannada Venus name is ಬೆಳ್ಳಿ beḷḷi, entered separately.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: Tadbhava of tārakā, thoroughly naturalised; forms the compound tārage-vaṭṭe 'the starry path, the sky'.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ತಾರಗೆ tārage, p. 752
entries.quote: ತಾರಗೆ tārage. Tbh. of ತಾರಕೆ. a star (ಮೀನ್ Ct. I, 46; ತಾರಕಿ II, 13; ಮೀನ್, ಅಱಿಲ್, ನಕ್ಷತ್ರ Kk. 10b; ಮೀನ್, ಅಱಿಲ್, ತಾರೆ Śm. 16 …). 2, one of the lunar mansions (ಮೃಗ, ನಕ್ಷತ್ರ Nn. 81). 3, another lunar mansion (ಪುಷ್ಯ, ನಕ್ಷತ್ರಭೇದ 130). -ತಾರಗೆಯಾಳ್ಮ. -ಆಳ್ಮ. the moon (Śm. 15). -ತಾರಗೆವಟ್ಟೆ. -ಬಟ್ಟೆ. the starry path, the sky (ಆಗಸ Śmd. II; Kk. 88).
entries.notes: Kittel records that some nighaṇṭus use ತಾರಗೆ as a name for particular nakṣatras — Mṛgaśiras in one, Puṣya in another. Those secondary uses are unusual and are not treated here as separate entries.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: The almanac and horoscope word; Kittel glosses it with the two Dravidian words, ಅಱಿಲ್ and ಮೀನ್.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ನಕ್ಷತ್ರ nakṣatra, p. 879
entries.quote: ನಕ್ಷತ್ರ nakṣatra. a star. (ಅಱಿಲ್, ಮೀನ್ Kk. 80). 2, a constellation, an asterism in the moon's path, a lunar mansion, of which 27 (or 28) are enumerated and regarded as the wives of the moon and daughters of Dakṣa. 3, the number 27 (ಇಪ್ಪತ್ತೇೞ್ Mr. 348).
entries.notes: This entry is the source for the summary statement that Kannada carries the full 27-fold nakṣatra system: Kittel gives all 27 as separate headwords in Kannada phonological shape.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಋಕ್ಷ r̥kṣa, p. 269
entries.quote: ಋಕ್ಷ ṛikṣa. = ರುಕ್ಷ 2. a bear. 2, a star; a constellation, a lunar mansion. 3, the plant Bignonia indica (ದಿಣ್ಡಲಮರ G.). 4, N. of a mountain.
entries.notes: Kittel preserves the Sanskrit bear/star polysemy intact. Telugu రిక్క rikka is the Middle-Indic descendant of the same word, but by Brown's time it means simply 'star' and has lost the bear.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಉಡು uḍu 6, p. 225
entries.quote: ಉಡು uḍu. a star. 2, water. (My.).
entries.notes: HOMONYM: Kittel has six headwords ಉಡು on this page — 'to wrap round the waist', 'the waist', 'iguana' and so on. Only the sixth is the star.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: Names the mansion by its position at the head of the list.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. తొలుత toluta, p. 562
entries.quote: తొలురిక్క the first constellation, i.e., Asvini. తొలువేలుపు the first god, i.e., Brahma సురజ్యేష్ఠుడు
entries.notes: This is one of a complete set of Telugu descriptive names for the lunar mansions that Brown records piecemeal under their first elements. They are formed X-cukka / X-rikka ('X-star') or X-rūpu-rikka ('X-shaped star'), and are entirely independent of the Sanskrit names, which Telugu also has.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: A translation, not a borrowing: the Sanskrit name is 'the two horsemen', and Telugu renders the horse with its own word gurramu.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. గుర్రము gurramu, p. 381
entries.quote: గుర్రపు వాసము gurrapu-vāsamu. n. A prop in the roof of a house. గుర్రపుచుక్క a certain star అశ్వినీనక్షత్రము.
entries.notes: This is one of a complete set of Telugu descriptive names for the lunar mansions that Brown records piecemeal under their first elements. They are formed X-cukka / X-rikka ('X-star') or X-rūpu-rikka ('X-shaped star'), and are entirely independent of the Sanskrit names, which Telugu also has. Here the calque is transparent: Aśvinī 'the Aśvins, horsemen' → gurrapu-cukka 'horse star'.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: The Sanskrit name Bharaṇī has been reshaped in Telugu onto the native word baraṇi 'casket, jewel-box', and Brown enters the asterism under that word.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. బరణి baraṇi, p. 873
entries.quote: బరణి … A casket, small jewel-case, snuff box, pill box. కటాటము. పాచికలబరిణ a dice-box. బరణిచుక్క or భరణి bharaṇi-ṭsukka. n. The second lunar mansion consisting of three stars in a triangle.
entries.notes: A folk-etymological reshaping rather than an independent formation: registered 'folk' for that reason. Brown's separate Sanskrit headword భరణి (p. 924) gives the same gloss, 'three stars in a triangle'.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: The Pleiades period as the farmer and almanac-user knows it; Brown attaches the solar season directly to the word.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. కత్తెర kattera, p. 238
entries.quote: కత్తెర [Tel.] n. Scissors. The constellation or sign called కృత్తిక. The period of time when the sun is between the signs భరణి, రోహిణి and కృత్తిక. … కత్తెరయెండ kattera-yeṇḍa. n. Fierce heat.
entries.notes: The cutting figure survives from Sanskrit kṛt- 'to cut' but is re-lexicalised on the native word kattera 'scissors'. The derived kattera-yeṇḍa 'fierce heat' shows the name doing seasonal work: the Kṛttikā period is the hot season in the Telugu country.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: A second, purely descriptive Telugu name for the Pleiades, from the shape of the cluster.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. మంగల mangala, p. 937
entries.quote: మంగల [Tel.] n. The barber caste. మంగలకత్తి mangala-katti. n. A razor, క్షురము. మంగలకత్తిరూపు the constellation called కృత్తికానక్షత్రము.
entries.notes: This is one of a complete set of Telugu descriptive names for the lunar mansions that Brown records piecemeal under their first elements. They are formed X-cukka / X-rikka ('X-star') or X-rūpu-rikka ('X-shaped star'), and are entirely independent of the Sanskrit names, which Telugu also has. With kattera 'scissors' this makes two independent Telugu names for the Pleiades built on a cutting-blade image.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: Named from the V of the Hyades, seen as a bullock cart.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. బండి banḍi, p. 864
entries.quote: బండి [Tel.] n. A cart, gig, carriage, coach, waggon, శకటము. … బండిమొగ్గరము banḍi-moggaramu. n. A certain military evolution called శకటవ్యూహము, which is shaped like a cart. బండిరిక్క banḍi-rikka. n. The star called రోహిణి.
entries.notes: The single best Telugu-Sanskrit correspondence in this file. The Sanskrit database has the same figure under 'rohini-shakata' (Rohiṇī-śakaṭa / Prājāpatya śakaṭa, 'the Wain of Rohiṇī' = the Hyades V with Aldebaran). Brown's Telugu word for it is baṇḍi, the ordinary Dravidian word for a bullock cart, not a rendering of śakaṭa; his own gloss for the military formation śakaṭa-vyūha on the same line shows he knew the two words were equivalents. Telugu preserved the cart independently.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: Built on jābili, the native Telugu word for the moon.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. జాబిల్లి ḍzābilli, p. 481
entries.quote: జాబిల్లి or జాబిలి [Tel. జాను+పిల్లి, i.e., చెవులపిల్లి.] n. The moon. చంద్రుడు. … జాబిలిరిక్క the constellation called మృగశీర్ష.
entries.notes: This is one of a complete set of Telugu descriptive names for the lunar mansions that Brown records piecemeal under their first elements. They are formed X-cukka / X-rikka ('X-star') or X-rūpu-rikka ('X-shaped star'), and are entirely independent of the Sanskrit names, which Telugu also has. Motivation uncertain: possibly because Mṛgaśiras is the mansion in which the moon's month Mārgaśīrṣa is full, or from the deer that the Sanskrit name and the Telugu word for the moon (jābili, glossed by Brown from the hare in the moon) share.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: A colour name.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. పగడపు జిట్ట pagaḍapu-jiṭṭa, p. 695
entries.quote: పగడపు జిట్ట n. A kind of bird. పక్షివిశేషము. పగడపురిక్క pagaḍapu-rikka. n. The constellation called అర్ద్రానక్షత్రము.
entries.notes: This is a genuine observational name and not a translation of anything Sanskrit. Ārdrā is Betelgeuse, one of the two reddest bright stars in the sky, and pagaḍamu is coral, i.e. red. Brown corroborates the equation coral = bright star at మెరుగు p. 1031, where merugu-rikka is glossed both 'Coral' and 'A bright star'.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. పొద poda, p. 813
entries.quote: పొదరిల్లు po ar-illu. (పొదరు+ఇల్లు.) n. A bower or arbour. నికుంజము. పొదరు Same as పొద. పొదరిండ్ల చుక్క the constellation called పునర్వసు నక్షత్రము.
entries.notes: This is one of a complete set of Telugu descriptive names for the lunar mansions that Brown records piecemeal under their first elements. They are formed X-cukka / X-rikka ('X-star') or X-rūpu-rikka ('X-shaped star'), and are entirely independent of the Sanskrit names, which Telugu also has. podaru-illu is 'bush-house, arbour'; the plural genitive gives 'star of the arbours'. Motivation unexplained by Brown.

entries.sky_object: Punarvasu (7th lunar mansion) as a sowing season
entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: AGRICULTURAL. The asterism name has become the name of a crop: the early, inferior grain crop of the year sown in the Punarvasu period.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. పునాస punāsa, p. 773
entries.quote: పునాస or పునాసలు [from Skt. పునర్వసు, the name of a star or constellation.] n. The first crop of the year which consists of grain of an inferior kind, కొర్రలు, బొబ్బర్లు మొదలగు ధాన్యము.
entries.notes: Registered 'folk' because the word has left the sky entirely: in ordinary Telugu punāsa is a kind of harvest, and Brown has to supply the etymology to explain that it is a star at all. The clearest single instance in either language of a star-name naturalised into the agricultural vocabulary.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: The month name is formed from the same base: poṭla-pū-rikka-nela = Pauṣa.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. పొట్ల poṭla, p. 809
entries.quote: పొట్ల [Tel. lit: that which has spots. పొడలుకలది. cf. Tamil పొడలంగాయ.] n. The snake gourd, Momordica charantia. … పొట్లపూచుక్క poṭla-pū-ṭsukka. n. The constellation called పుష్యమి, పొట్లపూరిక్క నెల the month called పుష్యమాసము.
entries.notes: This is one of a complete set of Telugu descriptive names for the lunar mansions that Brown records piecemeal under their first elements. They are formed X-cukka / X-rikka ('X-star') or X-rūpu-rikka ('X-shaped star'), and are entirely independent of the Sanskrit names, which Telugu also has. Brown spells the star with -cukka and the month with -rikka in the same line, which shows the two star-words were freely interchangeable in these compounds.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. సప్పము sappamu, p. 1304
entries.quote: సప్పము [from Skt. సర్పము.] n. A serpent. సప్పపుచుక్క sappapu-ṭsukka. n. The star called అశ్లేష.
entries.notes: A calque on the presiding deity rather than on the name: Āśleṣā's devatā is the Sarpas, and the db has the Vedic alias 'sarpa' for exactly this asterism. sappamu is the tadbhava of sarpa, so the name is half-Sanskrit; registered 'vernacular' because the compound itself is Telugu.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: Brown labels the register himself.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. అసిలేరు asilēru, p. 103
entries.quote: అసిలేరు [Tel.] n. A vulgar name for అశ్లేష the ninth lunar mansion.
entries.notes: The only place in either dictionary where the compiler explicitly grades a star-name for register. 'Vulgar' in Brown's usage means colloquial/rustic, hence 'folk' here. A worn-down popular form of Āśleṣā, not a new coinage.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. పెతరులు petarulu, p. 793
entries.quote: పెతరులు [from Skt. పితృలు.] n. plu. Forefathers or ancestors. పితృదేవతలు. పెతరులసామి the lord of the ancestors, i.e., Yama, యముడు. పెతరులచుక్క the constellation called మఘానక్షత్రము.
entries.notes: A calque on the presiding deity: Maghā's devatā is the Pitṛs, and petarulu is the Telugu tadbhava of pitṛ. The Telugu name is thus semantically transparent where the Sanskrit Maghā ('the bounties') is not.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: A ritual-calendar name: the asterism at whose appearance the yajñas fall due.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. జన్నము ḍzannamu, p. 476
entries.quote: జన్నము [from Skt. యజ్ఞము.] n. A sacrifice, a ceremony, in which oblations are presented. యజ్ఞము, వేలిమి. జన్నపుచుక్క a star or constellation on whose appearance sacrifices (యజ్ఞములు) are to be performed. మఘానక్షత్రము.
entries.notes: Second Telugu name for Maghā. jannamu is the tadbhava of yajña; the compound is Telugu. Note that Maghā is also called Makha in Sanskrit, and makha means 'sacrifice' — so this name may be a re-motivation of that variant rather than an independent observation.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. సాము sāmu, p. 1331
entries.quote: సాముకంటిచుక్క sāmu-kanṭi-ṭsukka. n. The name of a constellation called పుబ్బా or పూర్వఫల్గునీనక్షత్రము.
entries.notes: Literal meaning uncertain and therefore left null rather than guessed: Brown's headword సాము carries three unrelated senses on the same page ('a half', 'bodily exercise / fencing'), and he does not say which underlies the star-name. kaṇṭi is 'eye'.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: The everyday Telugu form of the name, marked [Tel.] by Brown against the tatsama పూర్వఫల్గుని.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. పుబ్బ pubba, p. 774
entries.quote: పుబ్బ [Tel.] n. The name of the eleventh lunar mansion.
entries.notes: COGNATE PAIR: Kannada has the identical worn form ಪುಬ್ಬೆ pubbe / ಹುಬ್ಬೆ hubbe, which Kittel derives 'Tbh. of ಪೂರ್ವೆ' (p. 1053, 1745). Sanskritic in origin, but the shape is the shared Deccan vernacular one, and Brown flags it [Tel.] for that reason.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: The month Phālguna is named from it in the same vernacular shape: proddu-rikka-nela.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. ప్రొద్దు proddu, p. 856
entries.quote: ప్రొద్దు or పొద్దు [Tel.] n. The sun, సూర్యుడు. … ప్రొద్దురిక్క proddu-rikka. n. A constellation called ఉత్తరఫల్లునీనక్షత్రము. ప్రొద్దురిక్క నెల proddu-rikka-nela. n. A name of the Telugu month called ఫాల్గుణమాసము.
entries.notes: A calque on the deity: Uttara-Phalgunī's devatā is Aryaman, an Āditya, i.e. a sun-god. proddu is the ordinary Dravidian word for sun/daytime. The fact that Telugu also names the whole month from it (proddu-rikka-nela = Phālguna) shows the vernacular nomenclature was a working calendar, not a poetic ornament.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: The month Caitra is named from it: muttepu-rikka-nela.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. ముత్తెము muttemu, p. 1008
entries.quote: ముత్తెము, ముత్తియము or ముత్యము [from Skt. మౌక్తికము.] n. A pearl. … ముత్తెపురిక్క నెల muttepu-rikka-nela. n. An epithet applied to the month, చైత్రమాసము. ముత్తెపుసవతు muttepu-savatu. n. The lunar mansion called చిత్రానక్షత్రము.
entries.notes: A colour/brilliance name and an excellent one — Spica is the brightest star of Virgo and is white. Brown gives the star itself as ముత్తెపుసవతు muttepu-savatu (savatu 'co-wife'), and only the month as muttepu-rikka-nela; the star-name muttepu-rikka is inferred from the month form. Both are recorded here under the -rikka form with the savatu variant quoted.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. కరువలి karuvali, p. 252
entries.quote: కరువలి [Tel.] n. Wind, air. గాలి, వాయువు. కరువలిపట్టి Bhīma or Hanuman. కరువలిరిక్క The Star Arcturus, స్వాతీ నక్షత్రము. కరువలివిందు Fire అగ్ని, వాయుసఖుడు.
entries.notes: A calque on the deity — Svāti's devatā is Vāyu — with the native Telugu word karuvali for wind. Compare the Sanskrit aliases in the db under 'pavana-svati' (Pavana / Anila / Vāyavya), which do exactly the same thing in Sanskrit. One of the few places where Brown gives the modern identification himself ('The Star Arcturus').

entries.sky_object: Svāti (15th lunar mansion) as a rain-period
entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: AGRICULTURAL/SEASONAL. The kārte of Svāti, thirteen days of the sun in October-November; and the pearl-oyster belief attached to it.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. స్వాతి svāti, p. 1384
entries.quote: స్వాతి [Skt.] n. Arcturus, the fifteenth lunar asterism. చిత్తకు అవలలినక్షత్రము, పదిహేనో నక్షత్రము. స్వాతికర్తి the fifteenth counstellation in which the sun happens to be for thirteen days in the month of October or November. స్వాతి చిప్పలు the oysters that gaps expecting drops of rain in Swāti.
entries.notes: svāti-cippalu, 'the oysters that gape expecting drops of rain in Svāti', is the Telugu form of the pan-Indian belief that a raindrop falling in Svāti becomes a pearl. Registered folk because kārte and the oyster proverb belong to the popular almanac, not the śāstra.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. కుమ్మర kummara, p. 296
entries.quote: కుమ్మర [Tel.] n. The potter's caste. … కుమ్మరసాన, or కుమ్మరసారె kummara-sāna n. A potter's wheel. కుమ్మరసారె చుక్క kummara-sārc-ṭsukka. n. The The name on the constellation called విశాఖానక్షత్రము.
entries.notes: A shape name with no Sanskrit model: Viśākhā means 'forked/branched'. The Telugu sees a potter's wheel. Brown's line has two typographical faults ('sārc' for sāre, 'The The name on the constellation'), reproduced verbatim above.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.literal_meaning: the star of the paired gods
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. జోడు ḍzōḍu, p. 485
entries.quote: జోడు [Tel.] n. A pair, or couple, a pair of shoes or sandals. Junction, conjunction. … జోడువేల్పులరిక్క the double star called విశాఖ.
entries.notes: A calque on the deity: Viśākhā's devatā is the dual Indrāgnī, and vēlpu is the native Telugu word for a god. Second Telugu name for the same mansion, built on the dual deity where kummara-sāre-cukka is built on the shape.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: The month Jyeṣṭha is named from it: tāṭi-rikka-nela.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. తాటి tāṭi, p. 521
entries.quote: తాటి or తాడి [Tel. Infl. of తాడు.] adj. Belonging to the palmyra tree. … తాటిరిక్క the constellation called జ్యేష్ఠా. తాటిరిక్కనెల the month called జ్యేష్ఠి మాసము.
entries.notes: This is one of a complete set of Telugu descriptive names for the lunar mansions that Brown records piecemeal under their first elements. They are formed X-cukka / X-rikka ('X-star') or X-rūpu-rikka ('X-shaped star'), and are entirely independent of the Sanskrit names, which Telugu also has. Motivation not stated by Brown; the palmyra fruits in Jyeṣṭha in the Telugu country, which is the likeliest link, but this is inference and is not asserted here.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: Mūla is the most inauspicious of the mansions in popular Telugu reckoning, and the name says so.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. సోకు sōku, p. 1366
entries.quote: సోకు [Tel.] v. n. To touch, come in contact with. … To be possessed by a demon, to be affected by the evil influence of stars or demons, గ్రహమావేశించు. … n. … An evil spirit, a demon, రాక్షసుడు, పిశాచము. … సోకుచుక్క the constellation called మూలనక్షత్రము. … సోకులరేడు sōkularēḍu. n. The regent of the S. W. region నైరృతి, మూలరేడు.
entries.notes: Internally consistent and self-verifying: Mūla's presiding deity is Nirṛti, and Brown's own next-but-one sub-entry glosses సోకులరేడు 'lord of the demons' as నైరృతి / మూలరేడు 'lord of Mūla'. So the Telugu name is a calque on the deity, made with the native word sōku 'evil spirit'.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. నీరు nīru, p. 670
entries.quote: నీటియిక్క nīṭi-yikka. n. A jewel worn on the breast of Vishṇu. కాస్తుభము. నీటిరిక్క nīṭi-rikka. n. The constellation called పూర్వాషాఢా నక్షత్రము. నీటిరేడు or నీటిరాయుడు nīṭi-rēḍu. n. Varuna, the god of the Ocean. నీటిరేనిరిక్క nīṭi-rēni-rikka. n. The constellation called శతభిత్తు.
entries.notes: A calque on the deity: Pūrvāṣāḍhā's devatā is Āpas, the Waters. The db has the parallel Sanskrit individual-star entry 'apas'. Note that Brown gives the water-king's star (nīṭi-rēni-rikka = Śatabhiṣaj, deity Varuṇa) in the very next line, so the two water-mansions are systematically distinguished in Telugu by 'water' vs 'water-king'.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. మద్దెల maddela, p. 955
entries.quote: మద్దెల [from Skt. మృదంగ.] n. A small drum. మృదంగము. మద్దెలరూపురిక్క maddela-rūpu-rikka. n. A constellation called ధనిష్ఠానక్షత్రము.
entries.notes: A shape name that agrees with the pan-Indian iconography of Dhaniṣṭhā as a drum, but built with the Telugu word maddela (< mṛdaṅga) and the Telugu formant -rūpu-rikka 'shaped star'. Compare mīnu-rūpu-rikka for Revatī below: -rūpu-rikka is a productive Telugu pattern for shape-named asterisms.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. నీరు nīru, p. 670
entries.quote: నీటిరేడు or నీటిరాయుడు nīṭi-rēḍu. n. Varuna, the god of the Ocean. నీటిరేనిరిక్క nīṭi-rēni-rikka. n. The constellation called శతభిత్తు.
entries.notes: A calque on the deity Varuṇa, using the native compound nīṭi-rēḍu 'king of the waters' which Brown himself defines two words earlier. The db has the Sanskrit aliases 'varuna-shatabhishaj' and 'pracetas-shatabhishaj' for the same equation. Note Brown's spelling శతభిత్తు for Śatabhiṣaj — the popular Telugu form.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. ముక్కంటి muk-kanṭi, p. 999
entries.quote: ముక్కంటి [Tel. from ముక్కన్ను (మూడు + కన్ను.] n. The three-eyed one; a title of Siva. త్రినేత్రుడు, త్రిలోచనుడు. ముక్కంటిచుక్క muk-kanṭi-ṭsukka. n. A constellation called ఉత్తరభద్రపద.
entries.notes: A calque on the deity: Uttara-Bhādrapadā's devatā is Ahirbudhnya, identified with Śiva/Rudra. mukkaṇṭi is a wholly Dravidian formation (mūḍu 'three' + kannu 'eye').

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. మీను mīnu, p. 996
entries.quote: మీను [Tel. A Drav: word common to all South Indian languages.] n. A fish. చేప. మీనురూపురిక్క a constellation called రేవతీ నక్షత్రము. plu. మీలు. మీనము mīnamu. [borrowed by Skt. from the Drav. languages.] n. A fish, మత్స్యము. The sign Pisces. మీనరాశి.
entries.notes: The one place Telugu mīnu touches the sky. Brown's headnote — 'A Drav: word common to all South Indian languages' — is the same word that in Kannada means 'star' outright (ಮೀನ್, Kittel p. 1328). Here Telugu uses it only for the shape of Revatī, i.e. Pisces. That contrast, mīn = 'star' in Kannada but only 'fish' in Telugu, is one of the sharper Telugu/Kannada differences in this file.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.literal_meaning: the end star, the last star
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. కొన kona, p. 319
entries.quote: కొన [Tel.] n. The end, extremity, termination, point, tip. చివర. … adj. Last. కొనవాడు the last man. … కొనరిక్క a certain constellation: రేవతీనక్షత్రము.
entries.notes: The positional counterpart of tolu-rikka 'the first star' (Aśvinī). The pair tolu-rikka / kona-rikka brackets the whole vernacular list and shows it was handled as an ordered sequence in Telugu, not just borrowed name by name.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: A star-count name: Revatī is reckoned at 32 stars.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. ముప్పది mup-padi, p. 1013
entries.quote: ముప్పది [Tel. మూడు + పది.] n. Thirty. త్రింశత్. ముప్పదిరెంటి గుంపు an epithet applied to a lunar mansion called రేవతీనక్షత్రము
entries.notes: Third Telugu name for Revatī, and the only star-count name in the vernacular set. The figure 32 for Revatī is the standard Indian one.

entries.sky_object: kārte — the solar period of a nakṣatra
entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: AGRICULTURAL. The unit of the Deccan farming calendar: the roughly thirteen days the sun spends in each of the 27 asterisms. Brown marks it [Tel.], not [Skt.].
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. కార్తె kārte, p. 276
entries.quote: కార్తె [Tel.] n. The particular constellation out of the 27, in which the Sun happens to be. ఇరువైయేడు కార్తెలు అనగా అశ్విని మొదలైన నక్షత్రములలో సూర్యుడు ఉండే దినాలు.
entries.notes: The single most consequential vernacular sky-word in either language, because sowing, weeding and harvest are timed by it. The word is the Telugu/Kannada Deccan development of Sanskrit kārttika; Kittel has no ಕಾರ್ತೆ headword, but the same system is documented for Kannada-speaking Bellary by Thurston (entered separately). Telugu also compounds it directly with an asterism name: svāti-karti (Brown p. 1384).

entries.sky_object: the 27 kārte as a sowing and rainfall calendar
entries.region: Bellary district, Deccan (Kannada- and Telugu-speaking Lingāyat cultivators)
entries.name_roman: Rohini Karte (and the rest of the 27 kārte)
entries.usage_note: AGRICULTURAL. Which crop is sown on which asterism's rain, and which asterism must not bring wind or lightning. Recorded for Lingāyat cultivators of Bellary.
entries.citation: Thurston, E. (assisted by K. Rangachari), Castes and Tribes of Southern India (Madras: Government Press, 1909), vol. IV, article 'Lingāyat', p. 290
entries.quote: Rain in Rohini Karte (one of the twenty-seven asterisms in which rain falls) is good for sowing, and that in Mrugasira and Ardra appropriate. These three asterisms are suited for sowing cholam. Showers in Punarvasu, Pushya, and Aslesha are suitable for sowing korra, saju and savi. Rain in Pubba and Wuttara is favourable to cotton, korra and horse gram, and that in Hasta and Chitta to wheat, cholam, Bengal gram and kusumulu (oil-seed). … In Magha, weeding, either by the hand or by bullocks, should not be done. Wind should not blow in Wuttara. … There should be no lightning flashes in Swati. … Rain in Visakha destroys worms, and is good for pulses. Rain in Anuradha spoils them.
entries.notes: name_native is null: Thurston prints these romanised only, and back-transliterating into Telugu or Kannada script would be inventing evidence — the district is bilingual and the informants were Lingāyats of Bellary, so it is not even certain which script would be right. The forms are the vernacular ones (Pubba, Wuttara, Chitta), not the Sanskrit ones. This passage is the best single demonstration that the nakṣatra list in the Deccan is a working agricultural instrument rather than a borrowed literary ornament.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: Also వేగురుచుక్క vēguru-cukka and వేకువచుక్క vēkuva-cukka. The standard Telugu name.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. వేగు vēgu, p. 1226
entries.quote: వేగుచుక్క, వేగురు చుక్క or వేకువచుక్క vēga-ṭsukka. n. The morning star, the planet Venus, శక్రుడు, వేగుజాము vēgu-dzāmu. n. The morning watch. రాత్రి నాలుగవజాము, వేకువజాము తెల్లవారుజాము.
entries.notes: Independently attested from the Kannada side: Kittel cites it under ಬಯ್ಗು baygu (p. 1143) as 'Te. ವೇಗುಜುಕ್ಕೆ, the morning star', in a comparative note on Dravidian *vaikV- 'to dawn'. Brown's Telugu gloss శక్రుడు is a misprint for శుక్రుడు (Śukra = Venus).

entries.sky_object: Venus as an unlucky star met on setting out
entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: Travel omen: a journey begun with this star facing you will go badly.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. చుక్క ṭsukka, p. 449
entries.quote: చుక్కవాలు ṭsukka-vālu. n. An evil planet or unlucky star. Particularly of Venus (ఛ?ుక్క, i.e., శుక్రః) for the Hindus believe that every journey will turn out ill if on setting out this star faces them.
entries.notes: Brown's parenthesis is garbled in the DSAL text ('ఛ?ుక్క'); the point he is making is that cukka here is a reshaping of Śukra. Compare Kittel s.v. ಬಾಲ (p. 1173), who cites 'Te. ವಾಲುಚುಕ್ಕೆ, the planet Venus, ಶುಕ್ರ' — the same compound with the elements reversed. Brown's own related sub-entry చుక్కయెదురు 'a star full in front' names the same omen.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: The ordinary Telugu word for a comet, still current.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. తోక tōka, p. 563
entries.quote: తోకచుక్క tōka-ṭsukka. n. A comet: a star with a tail. ధూమకేతువు.
entries.notes: COGNATE PAIR: Kannada ಬಾಲಚಿಕ್ಕಿ bālacikki / ಬಾಲಚುಕ್ಕೆ bālacukke, also 'tail-star' (Kittel p. 1173). Two languages, the same compound, built from different native words for 'tail' (Te. tōka, Ka. bāla). Sanskrit uses dhūmaketu 'smoke-bannered', a different image; both dictionaries gloss the vernacular word with it.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. దుమగతికేతు duma-gati-kētu, p. 602
entries.quote: దుమగతికేతు [Tel.] n. A star portending ill-luck. A comet, ధూమకేతువు.
entries.notes: Brown marks it [Tel.] although it is visibly a Telugu-ised remaking of Sanskrit dhūmaketu (duma < dhūma 'smoke'). Registered vernacular on Brown's own labelling, with the caveat that the material is Sanskrit.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: Not a name for a body but the idiom for the motion: a meteor falls 'cow-tail-wise', i.e. slanting and tapering.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. ఆదోకగా ādōka-gā, p. 114
entries.quote: ఆదోకగా [Tel. ఆవు+తోక] adv. Like a cow's tail. Slanting, in a slanting form, taperingly; conical, pyramidical A. iii. 30. నక్షత్రము ఆదోకపాటుగా పడుచున్నది the shooting star passes in a slanting direction.
entries.notes: Included because it is a genuinely observational vernacular usage rather than a nomenclature item; the head-word is ādōka-gā, and ādōka-pāṭu is the form in the illustrative sentence. Brown's etymology āvu + tōka 'cow + tail' is printed in the entry.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. ధ్రువుడు dhruvuḍu, p. 626
entries.quote: ధ్రువుడు or ధ్రువనక్షత్రము dhruvuḍu. n. The name of the North Pole: the Pole Star.
entries.notes: No vernacular Telugu pole-star name is recorded by Brown; the Sanskrit name is used unaltered. Note the DSAL headword for this page is misprinted as ధ్యానము. Same situation in Kannada (ಧ್ರುವ, Kittel p. 877).

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: The heliacal rising (agastyōdayamu) is an almanac event in the Telugu country.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. అగస్త్యుడు agastyuḍu, p. 24
entries.quote: అగస్త్యశాకము the leaves of a leguminous tree which are dressed and eaten, అనిసెచెట్టు; అగస్త్యనక్షత్రము the star Canopus. అగస్త్యచారము the cource of Canopus. అగస్త్యాదయము the rise of Canopus.
entries.notes: No vernacular name for Canopus in either dictionary — the Sanskrit sage-name is used in both languages (Kannada ಅಗಸ್ತ್ಯ, Kittel p. 12). Given the star's importance in the southern sky this is a real negative finding.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. నక్షత్రము nakshatramu, p. 628
entries.quote: నక్షత్రవీధి nakshatra-vīdhi. n. The Milky Way.
entries.notes: Brown gives only this Sanskrit compound for the Milky Way; his ఆకాశగంగ (p. 107) he glosses merely 'the river of heaven'. The vernacular Telugu names for the galaxy (pāla-punta etc.) are recorded only in the twentieth-century dictionaries — see the Gwynn entry.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: Also పాలబాట pāla-bāṭa 'the milk road' and పాలవెల్లి pāla-velli.
entries.citation: Gwynn, J. P. L., A Telugu-English Dictionary (Delhi: Oxford University Press, 1991), s.v. పాలబాట, పాలపుంత pālabāṭa, pālapunta, p. 331
entries.quote: పాలబాట, పాలపుంత pālabāṭa, pālapunta paalabaaTa, paalapunta n. astron. milky way.
entries.notes: Gwynn 1991 is a copyrighted modern dictionary; the quote is limited to the bare lexical gloss and nothing is taken from his discussion. The name is not in Brown (1903), so on the evidence assembled here the milk-image Telugu names cannot be pushed back into the nineteenth century — that is a dating limit, not a claim that they are recent. Kannada solves the same problem with a different figure entirely: ಬಾಂಗೆಱೆ 'sky-tank'.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. చిత్రము chitramu, p. 415
entries.quote: చిత్రశిఖండి chitra-ṣikhanḍi. n. The constellation called the Great Bear.
entries.notes: COGNATE PAIR: Kittel has the identical entry in Kannada, ಚಿತ್ರಶಿಖಣ್ಡಿ (p. 646), also glossed as Ursa Major. Both are Sanskrit tatsamas; the db has the same name under 'citrashikhandin'.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. ఋషి ṛishi, p. 178
entries.quote: సప్తర్షులు means (1.) the "seven sages," viz., మరీచి, అత్రి, అంగీరుడు, పులస్త్యుడు, పులహుడు, క్రతువు, వసిష్ఠుడు; (or) కశ్యపుడు, అత్రి, భరద్వాజుడు, విశ్వామిత్రుడు, గౌతముడు, జమదగ్ని, వసిష్ఠుడు; (2) the constellation of the Great Bear.
entries.notes: NEGATIVE FINDING attached here: neither Brown nor Kittel records any Dravidian name for the Big Dipper — no plough, no cart, no bier, no seven sisters. Both give only saptarṣi and citraśikhaṇḍi. Searches of Brown and Kittel for 'Great Bear', 'Ursa', 'seven stars', 'plough' and 'wain' turned up nothing vernacular. This is the largest gap in the vernacular sky of both languages.

entries.sky_object: Arundhatī, shown to the bridal pair
entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.usage_note: Wedding ritual: the bridegroom invokes her and the star is pointed out to the couple.
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. అరుంధతి arundhati, p. 81
entries.quote: అరుంధతి … A star in the Pleiades. A marriage ceremonies అరుంధతి is invoked by the bridegroom as a pattern of conjugal excellence and the star in the Pleiades which represents the wife of Vasishtha is pointed out to the bridal pair.
entries.notes: IDENTIFICATION CONFLICT, flagged rather than resolved, and Brown turns out to be defensible. The standard identification, and the one in the Sanskrit database (db id 'arundhati'), is Alcor beside Mizar in Ursa Major, since Arundhatī is Vasiṣṭha's wife and Vasiṣṭha is Mizar. But the marriage mantra Thurston prints (Castes and Tribes, vol. I, 'Brahman', p. 289) puts her in the Pleiades in the same breath as in Ursa Major: the couple are 'shown Druva and Arundathi (the pole star and Ursa major)', and the verse then addresses 'she, Arundathi, who stands first among the six Krithikas (Pleiads), may she the eighth one, who leads the conjunction of the (moon with the) six Krithikas … Thou art the pillar of the stars.' Brown's 'a star in the Pleiades' is therefore reporting the ritual text, not blundering. Thurston elsewhere has south Indian officiants calling Arundhatī the pole star outright — vol. I p. 143 (Balija, 'they gaze at the pole-star (Arundati)'), vol. III p. 238 (Kāpu), vol. VII p. 179 (Toreya) and p. 307 (Valluvan) — which is a third, distinct popular equation. All three circulate; none is corrected here.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. తేలు tēlu, p. 554
entries.quote: తేలు [Tel.] n. A scorpion. తేలుమీను. a sort of fish. తేలురాసి tēlu-vāsi. n. The constellation Scorpio. వృశ్చికరాశi.
entries.notes: A zodiacal sign, not a nakṣatra, so no db id. Included because it is a rare case of a vernacular Telugu word (tēlu 'scorpion') replacing the Sanskrit element (vṛścika) in a calendrical term. Brown's romanisation 'tēlu-vāsi' is a misprint for tēlu-rāsi.

entries.region: Telugu country (Madras Presidency: Coastal Andhra, Rayalaseema, Telangana)
entries.citation: Brown, C. P., A Telugu-English Dictionary, new ed., thoroughly revised and brought up to date (Madras: Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, 1903), s.v. మెరుగు merugu, p. 1031
entries.quote: మెరుగురిక్క or మెరుగుడురిక్క merugu-rikka. n. Coral. పగడము. A bright star, కాంతిగలచుక్క.
entries.notes: Not an identified object. Recorded because it corroborates pagaḍapu-rikka (Ārdrā, 'the coral star'): Brown here has one word meaning both 'coral' and 'a bright star', which shows that in Telugu the coral image and stellar brilliance were interchangeable.

entries.sky_object: the star-gazer who fixes the auspicious hour
entries.region: Vizagapatam Agency hills (Konda Dora)
entries.usage_note: The office, not the object: among the hill Konda Doras the Chukkamusti fixes the day and the hour of a wedding.
entries.citation: Thurston, E. (assisted by K. Rangachari), Castes and Tribes of Southern India (Madras: Government Press, 1909), vol. III, article 'Konda Dora', p. 352
entries.quote: On an auspicious day fixed by the Chukkamusti (star-gazer), the bride is conducted to the home of the bridegroom. … On the same day, or the following morning, at a time settled by the Chukkamusti, the bridegroom, under the direction of a caste elder, ties the sathamanam (marriage badge) on the bride's neck.
entries.notes: name_native is null — Thurston romanises only, and the second element is not securely identifiable (musti 'fist' is the obvious candidate but Thurston does not analyse it), so no Telugu spelling is supplied here. The first element is unmistakably cukka 'star'. This is the clearest tribal-register attestation of the word found: cukka doing astronomical work outside both the Sanskrit almanac and the plains dictionary.

entries.region: Telugu country (Uppu Yerukala / Korava)
entries.usage_note: One of the intiperu (house/sept names) given by Uppu Yerukalas; the list also contains Bandi 'cart' and Thoka 'tail'.
entries.citation: Thurston, E. (assisted by K. Rangachari), Castes and Tribes of Southern India (Madras: Government Press, 1909), vol. III, article 'Korava (Yerukala)', p. 452
entries.quote: As examples of intiperu, or exogamous septs, the following, which were given by Uppu Yerukalas, may be cited: — … Dasari, Vaishnavite mendicant. Sukka, star. Kampa, bush of thorns. Avula, cows. Thoka, tail. Kanaga (Pongamia glabra). Bandi, cart.
entries.notes: name_native null: Thurston romanises only. Sukka is the Yerukala form of Telugu cukka. Confidence 'likely' rather than certain because the sept name may equally reflect the 'dot/mark' sense; Thurston's own gloss is 'star', which is what is recorded. Not a name for any particular object.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: The everyday Kannada name for Venus is simply the word for silver.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಬೆಳ್ಳಿ beḷḷi, p. 1217
entries.quote: ಬೆಳ್ಳಿ beḷḷi. the white metal: silver … Tu. ಬೊಳ್ಳಿ; T., M. ವೆಳ್ಳಿ, ಬೆಳ್ಳೈ ವೆಳ್ಳೆ; Te. ವೆಲ್ಲೆ, ವೆಣ್ಡಿ). … 2, the planet Venus (My.; T., M. ವೆಳ್ಳಿ).
entries.notes: The most clearly Dravidian planet-name in this file: Kittel's own comparative note shows the star sense is shared with Tamil and Malayalam veḷḷi. Telugu, per Kittel's same note, kept only the metal sense (వెల్లి / వెండి) and names Venus instead with vēgu-cukka or with reflexes of Śukra. So this is a Dravidian sky-word that Kannada kept and Telugu lost — the mirror image of the mīn case.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: Kittel's citation (J. 26,5) is to the Jaimini Bhārata, i.e. it is a literary attestation.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಸಂಜೆ sañje, p. 1564
entries.quote: ಸಂಜೆ sañje. = ಚಂಜೆ, ಸನ್ದೆ. Tbh. of ಸನ್ಧ್ಯೆ. evening. … — ಸಂಜೆದಾರಕಿ. -ತಾರಕಿ. an evening-star (J. 26, 5).
entries.notes: A Kannada compound of two naturalised words (sañje < sandhyā, tāraki < tārakā), so the material is Sanskrit but the formation is not. Kittel does not identify the body; on the evidence it is Venus, but he says only 'an evening-star', so no Bayer designation is asserted. No corresponding Kannada morning-star compound is recorded — for the morning star Kittel cites Telugu, not Kannada (s.v. ಬಯ್ಗು, p. 1143).

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: Also ಬಾಲಚುಕ್ಕೆ bāla-cukke. The colloquial Kannada word.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಬಾಲ bāla, p. 1173
entries.quote: — ಬಾಲಚಿಕ್ಕಿ. a comet (My.; ಧೂಮಕೇತು G.). … — ಬಾಲಚುಕ್ಕೆ. = ಬಾಲಚಿಕ್ಕಿ. (My.; Te. ವಾಲುಚುಕ್ಕೆ, the planet Venus, ಶುಕ್ರ).
entries.notes: COGNATE PAIR with Telugu తోకచుక్క tōka-cukka. Note the trap in the same line: the Telugu compound Kittel cites as a parallel, vālu-cukke, does NOT mean comet — it is Venus (cf. Brown's చుక్కవాలు, p. 449). Kannada bāla and Telugu vālu are the same word 'tail', but the two languages built different objects out of it.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಧೂಮಕೇತು dhūmakētu, p. 875
entries.quote: ಧೂಮಕೇತು dhūma-kētu. whose sign is smoke : agni, fire (ಪಾವಕ, ಅಗ್ನಿ Nn. 33; ಸಪ್ತಾರ್ಚಿ Mr. 489). 2, a meteor, a falling star; a very portentous object; a comet (ಮಹೋತ್ಪಾದ, ಮಹೋತ್ಪಾತ 33; ಮಹೋತ್ಪಾತ 489).
entries.notes: The learned counterpart of bāla-cikki, and the word both dictionaries use to gloss the vernacular one.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಉಲ್ಕಾಪಾತ ulkāpāta, p. 257
entries.quote: ಉಲ್ಕಾಪಾತ ulkā-pāta. falling of a star, meteor-shoot. (My.).
entries.notes: No vernacular Kannada meteor word surfaced. Telugu, by contrast, has the folk idiom ādōka-pāṭu 'falling cow-tail-wise' (Brown p. 114).

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಆಕಾಶಗಂಗೆ ākāśagaṅge, p. 146
entries.quote: ಆಕಾಶಗಂಗೆ ākāśa-gaṅge. the celestial Ganges, the milky way (ಬಾಂಗೆಱೆ G.; My.). 2, a cascade (My.).
entries.notes: The entry is worth having chiefly for its parenthesis: Kittel gives the Kannada equivalent ಬಾಂಗೆಱೆ from the nighaṇṭu he abbreviates G., which is how the vernacular name is reached. Same db id as Sanskrit Ākāśagaṅgā.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: A Dravidian figure for the galaxy: not a river but an irrigation tank, the standing water of the Karnataka countryside.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಬಾಂ- bām-, p. 1166
entries.quote: ಬಾಂ- bāṅ. ಬಾಙ್-. = ಬಾನ್ 3, etc. the sky. — ಬಾಂಗಡಲ್. -ಕಡಲ್. the sky-sea : the celestial Ganges (Rśv. 10, 82; Śśv. 3, 3). — ಬಾಂಗೆಱೆ. - ಕೆಱೆ. the sky-tank (Rśv. 12, 12; V. 3, 14).
entries.notes: The best genuinely indigenous Kannada sky-figure found. Both elements are Dravidian (bān 'sky', keṟe 'tank'). Confidence 'likely' rather than certain only because Kittel's ಬಾಂ- entry glosses it literally as 'sky-tank' without saying Milky Way; the equation with the galaxy comes from his ಆಕಾಶಗಂಗೆ entry (p. 146), where bāṅgeṟe is given as the Kannada equivalent. His illustrative citation from the Rājaśekhara-vilāsa makes the sense plain — ಬಾಂಗೆಱೆಯೊಳ್ ಮೀಂಗಳ್ … ಮುೞುಗುವನ್ತೆ ಅಡಂಗಿದುವು, the stars vanished as though fishes were diving in the sky-tank (Kittel s.v. ಅಡಂಗು, p. 32), which turns on mīn meaning both fish and star.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಬಾಂ- bām-, p. 1166
entries.quote: — ಬಾಂಗಡಲ್. -ಕಡಲ್. the sky-sea : the celestial Ganges (Rśv. 10, 82; Śśv. 3, 3).
entries.notes: Third member of the Kannada set bān-kaḍal 'sky-sea' / bān-keṟe 'sky-tank' / bān-toṟe 'sky-river' (the last at Kittel p. 1169, glossed 'the celestial Ganges'). All three are Dravidian compounds on bān 'sky' with a different body of water; Kittel equates the sea and river forms with the celestial Ganges, i.e. with Ākāśagaṅgā.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಬಾನ್ bān 3, p. 1169
entries.quote: — ಬಾನ್ದೊಱೆ. - ತೊಱೆ. the celestial Ganges [ಬಾನ್ದೊಱೆಯನೆ ಪೊತ್ತು ಗೌರಿಗೆ ಕವಲ್ದೊಱೆಗೆಯ್ಸಿದಂ Pb. 7, 75]; (Bp. 17, 11).
entries.notes: The Kannada calque nearest to Sanskrit Ākāśagaṅgā, but made of Dravidian material throughout. Kittel's ಬಾನ್ 3 entry also lists the sky-road synonyms ಮೀನ್ವಟ್ಟೆ and ಅಱಿಲ್ವಟ್ಟೆ, which is why the star-road words are entered separately above.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಸಪ್ತರ್ಷಿ saptarṣi, p. 1579
entries.quote: ಸಪ್ತರ್ಷಿ sapta-ṛiṣi. = ಸಪ್ತಋಷಿ. the seven great ṛiṣis: Marīci, Atri, Aṅgiras, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, and Vasiṣṭha … 2, the constellation Ursa major (the seven stars of which are supposed to be the seven great ṛiṣis, ಚಿತ್ರಶಿಖಣ್ಡಿ, ಋಷಿಯರ್ Mr. 39).
entries.notes: Kittel's Kannada gloss ಋಷಿಯರ್ ṛṣiyar 'the sages' (with the Kannada plural) is the closest thing to a vernacular form, and it is still the Sanskrit noun. No Dravidian name for the Dipper is recorded.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಚಿತ್ರಶಿಖಣ್ಡಿ citraśikhaṇḍi, p. 646
entries.quote: ಚಿತ್ರಶಿಖಣ್ಡಿ citra-śikhaṇḍi. having bright crests. 2, the saptarṣis or seven great ṛiṣis (Marīci, Atri, etc.) as represented in the seven principal stars of the constellation of ursa major (ಋಷಿಯರ್ Mr. 39); the constellaiion itself.
entries.notes: COGNATE PAIR with Brown's Telugu చిత్రశిఖండి (p. 415), glossed identically. Both languages take the name over unchanged from Sanskrit.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಅರುನ್ಧತಿ arundhati, p. 102
entries.quote: ಅರುನ್ಧತಿ arundhati. -ತೀ N. of the wife of Vasiṣṭha. (Ch. v. 8; Mr. 258; Bp. 4, 30; 11, 40; J. 13, 40). 2, N. of a star (My.).
entries.notes: Kittel does not identify the star, so the modern_star here is supplied from the Sanskrit database rather than from him; hence 'likely'. He does not repeat Brown's 'in the Pleiades' error.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಇಲ್ವಲೆಗಳ್ ilvalegaḷ, p. 206
entries.quote: ಇಲ್ವಲೆಗಳ್ ilvalegaḷ. (Sk. ಇಲ್ವಲಾಃ). the five stars in Orion's head.
entries.notes: The Sanskrit Ilvalāḥ / Invakāḥ with the Kannada plural -gaḷ, which is why the register is sanskritic but the form is Kannada. Kittel says five stars; the Vedic and later tradition, and the Sanskrit database entries 'ilvala' and 'invaka', give three (λ, φ¹, φ² Orionis). The discrepancy is recorded, not resolved; modern_star follows the standard three-star identification.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಕೃತ್ತಿಕೆ kṛttike, p. 491
entries.quote: ಕೃತ್ತಿಕೆ kṛittike. the third lunar mansion containing six stars called the Pleiades, who are considered to be the nurses of Kārttikēya. (B. 5, 308). 2, a vehicle, a cart. 3, N. of a utensil (ಬೀವು Mr. 207).
entries.notes: Note sense 2, 'a vehicle, a cart' — a stray cart-word sitting in the Pleiades entry, presumably by contamination with Sanskrit kṛtti/śakaṭa; it is not offered here as a star-name. Kannada has no Dravidian Pleiades name in Kittel: the alternatives he gives (ಬಹುಲೆಗಳ್, ಅಗ್ನಿದೇವೆ) are both Sanskrit.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಬಹುಲೆ bahule, p. 1159
entries.quote: ಬಹುಲೆ bahule. a cow. 2, large cardamoms. 3, ಬಹುಲೆಗಳ್, the Pleiades or kṛittikās.
entries.notes: Sanskrit Bahulāḥ (db id 'bahula') with the Kannada plural. HOMONYM: the same headword is 'a cow' and 'large cardamoms', so only the third sense is astronomical.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಅಗ್ನಿದೇವೆ agnidēve, p. 16
entries.quote: ಅಗ್ನಿದೇವೆ agni-dēve. the third lunar mansion, the Pleiades.
entries.notes: The deity-name type, matching Sanskrit Āgneya (db id 'agneya') and Telugu అగ్నినక్షత్రము (Brown p. 26, 'the Pleiades'). Present in both languages, borrowed in both.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಆಗ್ರಹಾಯಣಿ āgrahāyaṇi, p. 151
entries.quote: ಆಗ್ರಹಾಯಣಿ āgrahāyaṇi. N. of a lunar mansion, Mṛigaśiras (Orion).
entries.notes: The one place either dictionary names Orion as a constellation rather than a mansion, and it does so through a Sanskrit word. Neither Brown nor Kittel has any vernacular Orion or Orion's-Belt name; searches for 'Orion', 'three stars' and 'belt' in both dictionaries returned nothing indigenous. A significant negative finding.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಲುಬ್ಧಕ lubdhaka, p. 1440
entries.quote: ಲುಬ್ಧಕ lubdhaka. a greedy or avaricious man, a miser (ಕೃಪಣ, ದೀನ Nn. 127). 2, a huntsman (ಶಾಬರ, ಕಿರಾತ 127; ಕಣ್ಟಕ, ಬೇಡ Nn. 39). 3, the sixth (or eighth, My.). nakṣatra or lunar mansion (ಆರ್ದ್ರೆ, ಆರ್ದ್ರಾನಕ್ಷತ್ರ 127; ಆರ್ದ್ರೆ, ಪುಷ್ಯ Mr. 39). 4, the star Sirius.
entries.notes: HOMONYM WARNING, and an important one: in Kannada lexicography Lubdhaka is primarily the name of the mansion Ārdrā (Betelgeuse), and only in Kittel's fourth sense the star Sirius. The Sanskrit database keeps these apart as 'lubdhaka' (Sirius) and 'ardra' (Betelgeuse). Anyone reading a Kannada nighaṇṭu gloss ಲುಬ್ಧಕ = ಆರ್ದ್ರೆ as meaning Sirius would go wrong. Brown records no Sirius name in Telugu at all.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಅಗಸ್ತ್ಯ agastya, p. 12
entries.quote: ಅಗಸ್ತ್ಯ agastya. N. of a ṛiṣi (= ಅಗಸ್ತಿ No. 1; Bp. 19, 26). 2, the star Canopus or its regent. 3, = ಅಗಸೆ 1, q. v.
entries.notes: Also ಅಗಸ್ತಿ agasti (p. 12), 'the regent of the star Canopus'. As in Telugu, no vernacular name.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: Also ಧ್ರುವನಕ್ಷತ್ರ dhruva-nakṣatra, same page.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಧ್ರುವ dhruva, p. 877
entries.quote: ಧ್ರುವ dhruva. = ದರುವು, ಧೃವ. fixed, firm, fast, immovable … 3, the polar star; the north pole. 4, the trunk of a lopped tree; a post, stake. 5, a wooden roller used in an oil-mill …
entries.notes: HOMONYM: senses 4 and 5 (post, stake, oil-mill roller) are the ordinary Kannada uses; only sense 3 is the star. The shared image of the pole as a fixed post is the same one behind the Sanskrit meḍhī 'threshing-post' in the db.

entries.sky_object: the rope from the pole star
entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: COSMOLOGY. The earth is held up by a rope tied to the pole star.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಧ್ರುವಪಾಶ dhruvapāśa, p. 877
entries.quote: ಧ್ರುವಪಾಶ dhruva-pāśa. the rope by which the earth is suspended from the polar star (My.).
entries.notes: Registered folk because it is a popular cosmological belief rather than a name for anything, and because Kittel sources it to the Mysore colloquial (My.). It is the Kannada version of the pan-Indian image the Sanskrit database has as meḍhī / medhībhūta, 'the threshing-post to which the sky is tethered' (db id 'medhi') — but reversed: here it is the earth that hangs from the sky.

entries.sky_object: the pole star, as Dhruva son of Uttānapāda
entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಔತ್ತಾನಪಾದಿ auttānapādi, p. 344
entries.quote: ಔತ್ತಾನಪಾದಿ auttānapādi. (fr. ಉತ್ತಾನಪಾದ). N. of Dhruva, grandson of the first Manu. 2, the polar star.
entries.notes: Kittel's separate headword ಉತ್ತಾನಪಾದ (p. 230) is glossed 'N. of a star in the little bear', i.e. he distinguishes the father-star from the son-star; the Sanskrit database keeps the same pair ('uttanapada' as a Śiśumāra position, 'auttanapadi' as the pole).

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: The naturalised Kannada form is ಸಾತಿ sāti (p. 1613, 'Tbh. of ಸ್ವಾತಿ').
