entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಸ್ವಾತಿ svāti, p. 1692
entries.quote: ಸ್ವಾತಿ svāti. = ಸಾತಿ 1. an auspicious constellation; the star Arcturus as forming the fifteenth lunar asterism.
entries.notes: Compare Telugu, which has both this and a fully vernacular name for the same star, కరువలిరిక్క 'the wind star'. Kannada has only the borrowed name — a clean instance of the asymmetry this file is trying to document.

entries.sky_object: Pūrva-Phalgunī (11th lunar mansion) as a rain-star
entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: AGRICULTURAL. Kittel prints two Kannada proverbs on the Hubbe rains under the headword — the whole entry is quoted below.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಹುಬ್ಬೆ hubbe, p. 1745
entries.quote: ಹುಬ್ಬೆ hubbe. = ಉಬ್ಬೆ, ಪುಬ್ಬೆ. Tbh. of ಪೂರ್ವೆ. the eleventh Nakṣatra. (Śmd. 356; C.). ಹುಬ್ಬೇ ಮಳೆ ಗುಬ್ಬೀ ತಲೆ ನೆನೆಯುವುದಿಲ್ಲ. - ಹುಬ್ಬೇ ಮೞೆ ಅಬ್ಬೇ ಹಾಲು (Prv.).
entries.notes: The name itself is a tadbhava of Pūrvā and so sanskritic in origin, but it is entered here as folk because what Kittel actually records is proverbial rain-lore, not the almanac term: the first proverb says the Hubbe rain will not wet even a sparrow's head, the second calls it a mother's milk — the two verdicts sitting side by side, as proverbs about weather do. COGNATE PAIR with Telugu పుబ్బ pubba (Brown p. 774), the identical worn form.

entries.sky_object: Maghā (10th lunar mansion) as a rain-star
entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: AGRICULTURAL. Also ಮಘೆ maghe (p. 1256), which carries a second rain proverb.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಮಖೆ makhe, p. 1254
entries.quote: ಮಖೆ makhe. = ಮಘೆ. (My.). the tenth nakṣatra. ಮಖೆಮೞೆ ಆದರೆ ಮೊಗ ತೊಳೆಯುವದಕ್ಕೆ ಆಗದೇ? (Prv.).
entries.notes: Second Kannada rain-star proverb: if the Makhe rain falls, will it not do at least to wash one's face with? — i.e. the Maghā rain is slight. Kittel's parallel headword ಮಘೆ (p. 1256) prints ಮಘೇ ನೀರು ಮೊಗೇಲಿಡು !, on the same theme. Together with Hubbe these show that in Kannada the rain-lore attaches to the tadbhava asterism names themselves, where Telugu instead built a separate word, kārte, for the solar period.

entries.sky_object: Ārdrā (6th lunar mansion) as a season
entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: SEASONAL. The Ārdrā period is July-August in Kittel's reckoning, and an insect is named from it.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಆರಿದ್ರ āridra, p. 168
entries.quote: ಆರಿದ್ರ āridra. Tbh. of ಆರ್ದ್ರೆ. the sixth lunar mansion (My.; Mhr. ಆರದ್ರಾ. -ಆರಿದ್ರಪುಱು. the insect called lady-bird or maybug, so called because it appears in July and August, which season is called Ārdre (Te. ಆರುದ್ರೆಪುರುಗು, ಆರ್ದ್ರೆ; R.).
entries.notes: The clearest Kannada case of a nakṣatra name in ordinary rural use: the ladybird is the 'Ārdrā-worm' because it comes out in the Ārdrā rains. Kittel gives the Telugu equivalent ఆరుద్రపురుగు in the same breath, so the usage is shared across both languages — a genuine Telugu/Kannada folk pair. Registered folk rather than sanskritic because the reference is to the season, not the star.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: Kittel notes the mansion is held unlucky and prints a proverb on it.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಧನಿಷ್ಠೆ dhaniṣṭhe, p. 868
entries.quote: ಧನಿಷ್ಠೆ dhaniṣṭhe. (a very rich female); the twenty-third lunar mansion, (considered to be connected with ill-luck). ಅರಸನಿಗೂ ಧನಿಷ್ಠೆ, ನನಗೂ ಧನಿಷ್ಠೆ (Prv.).
entries.notes: The proverb — Dhaniṣṭhā for the king and Dhaniṣṭhā for me too — turns on the mansion's ill luck falling on rich and poor alike. Compare the Telugu vernacular name for the same mansion, మద్దెలరూపురిక్క 'the drum-shaped star'; Kannada keeps the Sanskrit name and attaches the folklore to it instead.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: The naturalised Kannada form; Kittel's tatsama headword ಚಿತ್ರೆ citre (p. 647) is the one that carries the identification 'spica virginis'.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಚಿತ್ತೆ citte, p. 646
entries.quote: ಚಿತ್ತೆ citte. Tbh. of ಚಿತ್ರೆ. the fourteenth lunar mansion. (C.; Te.). [ಚಿತ್ತೆಯ ಸರಿಯನ್ತೆಱಗಿ ಪೋದುದಮರ ಸಮಾಜಂ Ap. 14, 147].
entries.notes: REPRESENTATIVE FORM for the tadbhava series. Kittel marks it 'C.; Te.', i.e. common Kannada and shared with Telugu — and indeed Brown has చిత్త citta (p. 414) for the same mansion. The pair citte/citta is a good specimen of the shared Deccan vernacular shape of the nakṣatra list.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಜೇಟೆ jēṭe, p. 696
entries.quote: ಜೇಟೆ jēṭe. = ಜೆಷ್ಟೆ. Tbh. of ಜ್ಯೇಷ್ಠೆ (Śmd. 370).
entries.notes: REPRESENTATIVE FORM. Compare Telugu జెష్ట jeṣṭa (Brown p. 469), which Brown says has drifted from 'elder sister' to 'a plague, a pest, gibberish' — the same tadbhava, but in Telugu it has left the sky and become an insult. Kittel's tatsama ಜ್ಯೇಷ್ಠೆ (p. 701) is the astronomical one: 'the eighteenth lunar mansion, being a part of scorpio'.

entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಭರಣಿ bharaṇi, p. 1237
entries.quote: ಭರಣಿ bharaṇi. = ಬರಣಿ. a china jar or vase. 2, the second nakṣatra (My.).
entries.notes: COGNATE PAIR, and the same folk etymology in both languages: Kittel equates ಭರಣಿ with ಬರಣಿ 'a china jar or vase', exactly as Brown enters the Telugu asterism under బరణి 'a casket, jewel-case'. The container reading of Bharaṇī is therefore a shared Deccan vernacular development, not a Telugu quirk.

entries.sky_object: the sky, as the road of the stars
entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: One of three synonymous Kannada 'star-road' compounds: mīn-vaṭṭe, aṟil-vaṭṭe (p. 105), tārage-vaṭṭe (p. 752).
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಮೀನ್ mīn 2, p. 1328
entries.quote: — ಮೀನ್ವಟ್ಟೆ. -ಬಟ್ಟೆ. the sky (ಆಕಾಶ Kk. 12).
entries.notes: COGNATE PAIR with Telugu చుక్కలతెరువు cukkala-teruvu 'the street of the stars = the sky'. Both are formed star-word + road-word, in each case with the language's own material; Sanskrit tārāpatha (db id 'tarapatha') has the same figure but is not the source of either.

entries.sky_object: the moon, as lord of the stars
entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.usage_note: Also ತಾರಗೆಯಾಳ್ಮ tārageyāḷma, same sense, Kittel p. 752.
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಮೀನ್ mīn 2, p. 1328
entries.quote: — ಮೀನ್ಗಳೆಱೆಯ. -ಎಱೆಯ. the moon (ಚನ್ದಿರ, etc., ಶಶಿ Kk. 44).
entries.notes: COGNATE PAIR with Telugu చుక్కలరేడు cukkala-rēḍu 'king of the stars = the moon' (Brown p. 449). The kenning is shared with Sanskrit (nakṣatreśa, uḍupati — Brown glosses both with the Telugu compound), but the Kannada and Telugu words are built entirely from Dravidian material, and the Kannada one puns on mīn 'fish'.

entries.sky_object: the whole host of stars; the zodiac
entries.region: Karnataka (Mysore, Canara, Deccan)
entries.citation: Kittel, F., A Kannaḍa-English Dictionary (orig. Mangalore: Basel Mission, 1894); cited from the revised and enlarged edition, [Madras] University of Madras, 1968-71, as keyed for DSAL, s.v. ಭಗಣ bhagaṇa, p. 1234
entries.quote: ಭಗಣ bha-gaṇa. the whole multitude of stars or constellations (ದ್ವಿಜ, ನಕ್ಷತ್ರಂಗಳ್ Nn. 36; ನಕ್ಷತ್ರಂಗಳ್ 40; ಮೀನ್ Śm. 99); the zodiac. 2, N. of a metrical foot (Ch.).
entries.notes: Included for the parenthesis: the Kannada nighaṇṭu Śabdamaṇidarpaṇa glosses the Sanskrit collective bhagaṇa simply with ಮೀನ್, 'fish/star'. Brown has the same word in Telugu, భగణము (p. 922), 'An assemblage of stars'. HOMONYM: also a metrical foot in both languages.

caveats: KITTEL EDITION. The Kannada material is quoted from the text DSAL keys, which is the revised and enlarged edition of Kittel published by the University of Madras in 1968-71, not the Basel Mission first edition of 1894. The definitions are Kittel's own and the page numbers are those of the DSAL text; source_date is given as 1894 for the work, but anyone citing a page should use the citation string, which names the edition. The 1894 pagination has not been separately verified here, and the archive.org scans of the first edition OCR the Kannada script too badly to check it against.

BROWN EDITION. The Telugu material is the 1903 revision of Brown's dictionary (Society for Promoting Christian Knowledge, Madras), which is the DSAL text, not the 1852 first edition. Where the 1903 revisers added or altered an entry this cannot be detected from the DSAL text alone.

DSAL TYPOGRAPHY. The keyed DSAL text carries visible faults which are reproduced verbatim in the quotes rather than silently mended: 'kummara-sārc-ṭsukka' and 'The The name on the constellation' at Brown p. 296; 'tēlu-vāsi' for tēlu-rāsi at p. 554; 'the cource of Canopus' at p. 24; 'శక్రుడు' for శుక్రుడు at p. 1226; 'twenty lunar mansions' for twenty-seven at p. 628; the garbled 'ఛ?ుక్క' at p. 449; the headword for Brown p. 626 filed under ధ్యానము when the entry is ధ్రువుడు; 'constellaiion' at Kittel p. 646.

ROMANISATION. name_roman follows the source's own transliteration where the source gives one (Brown's ṭsukka is normalised to cukka, and Kittel's ar̤il to aṟil, for consistency within this file); where the source romanises only and prints no native script — the Thurston material — name_native is null and has NOT been back-transliterated.

GWYNN. Gwynn's Telugu-English Dictionary (1991) is in copyright. It is used for one entry only, the Telugu Milky Way, and the quote there is confined to the bare lexical gloss; nothing of his discussion is reproduced.

THE TELUGU DEŚYA SET IS BROWN'S, NOT A FIELD RECORD. Brown gives no source for these names and no indication of where or by whom they were used; they are likely to come from a Telugu nighaṇṭu tradition rather than from his own enquiry. Their currency in speech in 1852 or 1903 is not established by this evidence, only their currency in the lexicon.

GAZETTEERS NOT PRODUCTIVE. Mysore Gazetteer vol. I (Hayavadana Rao, 1927) was downloaded and searched: it contains no nakṣatra or kārti material. The Bellary agricultural star-calendar is therefore carried here on Thurston alone. District gazetteers for Hyderabad and the Telugu districts were not obtained.

REEVE/SANDERSON NOT USABLE. The Reeve-Sanderson Canarese-English Dictionary (1858) was downloaded from archive.org, but the OCR of the Kannada script is too corrupt to quote verbatim, so it contributes nothing and no entry rests on it. Sankaranarayana's Telugu-English Dictionary was not located in a usable full-text form.

IDENTIFICATIONS. modern_star for the lunar mansions is taken from the Sanskrit database's yogatārā identifications, not from Brown or Kittel, who almost never give one (the exceptions — Arcturus for Svāti, Spica for Citrā, Canopus for Agastya, Sirius for Lubdhaka, the Pleiades for Kṛttikā — are quoted where they occur). A vernacular name and its Sanskrit counterpart are assumed to denote the same star; where a source's own identification conflicts with that, as with Arundhatī, confidence is set to disputed and the conflict is stated.

REGISTER IS A JUDGEMENT. Only one name in the whole file is graded for register by its source: Brown calls asilēru 'a vulgar name'. Every other register tag is the compiler's, assigned on the word's material (Dravidian vs Sanskrit), its formation (native compound vs borrowing), and the source's own labelling ([Tel.], Tbh., My., Prv.). Names whose material is Sanskrit but whose compounding is not — sañje-tāraki, sappapu-cukka, jannapu-cukka, maddela-rūpu-rikka — are tagged vernacular, and the reasoning is stated in each entry's notes.
